canonicalExplanation.summary: Within a flex line, `align-self` overrides one item's cross-axis alignment, and `margin-inline-start: auto` pushes an item to the far end. `flex: 1` shares **free space**, but items still won't shrink below their min-content size unless you add `min-width: 0` — so "equal" columns can end up unequal. `order` and `row-reverse` change only the **visual** order: keyboard focus and screen readers still follow the HTML, so keep visual and source order matching.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A notification row has an icon, a message and a close button. A long message pushes the close button off-screen, and "fixing" it with `order: -1` makes the Tab key jump around unpredictably. A text item gets min-width:0 so it can shrink beside a fixed icon without overflowing. In this lesson you'll debug alignment and verify meaningful source and focus order.

```predict
{"question": "Three items all have `flex: 1`. One contains a very long unbreakable word. Are they equal widths?", "options": ["Always equal", "Not necessarily — the long word's min-content can force that item wider"], "answer": 1, "why": "flex: 1 shares free space, but automatic minimum sizes still apply. Add min-width: 0 (and let text wrap) for truly equal shares."}
```

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know **Normal flow and display**, **Intrinsic sizing and constraints**, **Flex axes and sizing**, and **Keyboard navigation and skip links** (keyboard order matters).

sections.heading: The rule: align individually, shrink deliberately, keep order honest
sections.body:
```css
.note { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.75rem; }
.note__icon  { flex: none; }                    /* fixed size */
.note__text  { flex: 1; min-width: 0; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
.note__close { margin-inline-start: auto; align-self: flex-start; }
```

| Tool | Effect |
|---|---|
| `align-self`. | one item's cross-axis alignment. |
| `margin-inline-start: auto`. | pushes the item to the end. |
| `min-width: 0`. | lets a flex item shrink below its content. |
| `order`, `row-reverse`. | visual order only — not focus order. |

```reveal
{"prompt": "Why is `order` risky?", "answer": "Keyboard Tab order and screen-reader reading order follow the DOM. If visuals say A-B-C but focus goes B-A-C, users get lost. Reorder the HTML instead."}
```

sections.heading: Check focus order

includes: Use align-self, auto margins and min-width: 0 to debug flex alignment and overflow.
Keep visual order matching source and focus order; avoid order for meaningful content.

outcomes: Debug alignment and verify meaningful source and focus order.

examples.title: Text that shrinks beside a fixed icon
examples.situation: A text item gets min-width:0 so it can shrink beside a fixed icon without overflowing.
walkthrough: **Problem:** a long message's min-content width pushes the close button out of the notification row.
**Fix:** the icon gets `flex: none`; the text item gets `flex: 1; min-width: 0; overflow-wrap: anywhere` so it can shrink and wrap.
**Verify:** at 320px the browser will render icon, wrapped text and close button inside the row, and Tab reaches the close button in source order.
examples.result: The fixed icon and close button stay visible while the text shrinks and wraps.

examples.title: The reordered form buttons
examples.situation: A dialog uses `flex-direction: row-reverse` so "Save" appears on the right, but HTML order is Save then Cancel.
walkthrough: Visually: Cancel, Save. Tab order: Save, Cancel.
Keyboard users hit Save first while expecting Cancel.
Fix: write the HTML as Cancel, Save and use `justify-content: flex-end` for placement.
examples.result: Visual, reading and focus order now match.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: flex:1 guarantees equal final widths regardless of content and minimum size.
misconceptions.correction: flex: 1 distributes free space, but items keep an automatic minimum size based on their content. Long content can make items wider unless min-width: 0 and wrapping are applied.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In the opening predict, what made one item wider?

analogy.example: Flex items sharing space are like **people sharing a bench**: everyone gets an equal share of the free space, but someone carrying a long plank (unbreakable content) still needs room — unless they're allowed to fold it (wrap) and squeeze (min-width: 0).
usefulFor: order changes seats, not the queue
limitations: People can negotiate; items follow fixed rules.
Moving seats (order) doesn't change who's first in the queue (focus).

steps.explanation: Long text sets a large automatic minimum.
The text item gets min-width:0 so it can shrink beside a fixed icon.
Nothing overflows, and focus follows the source order.

trace.textAlternative: Debugging a flex row. Step 1, Overflow: text min-content is wider than row; close button is off-screen. Long text sets a large automatic minimum. Step 2, Allow shrinking: min-width is 0; text is wraps. The text item gets min-width:0 so it can shrink beside a fixed icon. Step 3, Result: row is fits 320px; Tab order is message link, then close button. Nothing overflows, and focus follows the source order.

remediation.explanation: When a flex row misbehaves: **1) which item is too wide? → min-width: 0 + wrap. 2) Is anything visually reordered? → fix HTML order instead.**
remediation.retryPrompt: Apply both checks to "The reordered form buttons".

recap.summary: To debug alignment and verify meaningful source and focus order, use align-self and auto margins for placement, add min-width: 0 and wrapping so text can shrink beside fixed items, and avoid order/row-reverse for meaningful content — reorder the HTML instead.
